_comment: Device frame assets vendored from fastlane/frameit-frames (MIT license: https://github.com/fastlane/frameit-frames). offsetX/offsetY/screenshotWidth are pixel values from that repo's offsets.json, in the frame PNG's own coordinate space (top-left corner + width to resize the raw screenshot to, before compositing it behind the frame). screenshotHeight is the matching cutout height, measured from each frame PNG's alpha channel rather than assumed, so the screen box never depends on the raw capture's own aspect ratio. screenCornerRadius rounds the screenshot to the device's screen corners: these frames' cutouts are a plain rectangle whose corners can fall OUTSIDE the rounded device body (verified: alpha is 0 at all four corners of the iPhone cutout), so a square-cornered screenshot leaks past the bezel silhouette. outputWidth/outputHeight are Apple's exact required App Store Connect screenshot pixel sizes for this device's display class (developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/screenshot-specifications) - the final composited PNG must match exactly, no tolerance.

iPhone 17 Pro Max._comment: screenCornerRadius 186 is the real 17 Pro Max screen corner radius (~62pt @3x); the measured minimum that keeps every corner inside the bezel silhouette is 80, so this is both accurate and safe.

iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)._comment: frameit-frames has no frame for this exact model yet; standing in with 'iPad Pro (12.9-inch) (4th generation)' - its screen aspect ratio (2048/2732 = 0.7496) is within 0.1% of the 13-inch M5's native ratio (2064/2752 = 0.7500), so the composite has no visible gap or distortion. outputWidth/outputHeight (2048x2732) is one of the two Apple-accepted '13-inch Display' sizes and happens to equal this frame's own native screenshot width, so no scaling mismatch either. This frame's cutout is already rounded (measured 43px), so its corners are covered by the bezel either way; the radius is set to match rather than to rescue it.
